name: Safal Bora
milestone_by_age_26: In December 2024 at age 26 he crossed 2500 FIDE and completed FIDE Grandmaster requirements after earning his final GM norm in July 2024.
early_history_summary: Born May 19, 1998 in Troy, Michigan. Earned first GM norm at the Charlotte Chess Center in March 2016 (age 17), studied business and engineering at University of Michigan, and works as a Microsoft software engineer while competing. Final GM norm July 2024 (NYC Chess Norms) and 2500 rating threshold December 2024 sealed the GM title.
family_context_summary: Raised in Troy, Michigan; family financial and coaching details not richly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: junior chess norms, UMich dual degrees, Microsoft engineer dual path
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and US Chess report first GM norm March 2016, final GM norm July 2024, and 2500 rating December 2024 completing GM title at age 26. Software engineering role at Microsoft is documented but not the age-26 material milestone; chess GM is the dated competitive achievement. Family coaching and wealth details are thin in public sources.
starting_point: Born May 19, 1998 in Troy, Michigan; dual-tracked competitive chess and engineering studies at University of Michigan.
current_position: American chess Grandmaster (title ~2024–25) and software engineer at Microsoft.

trajectory.event: Earned first GM norm at Charlotte Chess Center GM invitational.
Represented University of Michigan at the Ivy Chess Challenge.
Final GM norm (July) and 2500 FIDE rating (December) completed Grandmaster title requirements.
Listed among American grandmasters while continuing software engineering work at Microsoft.

name: Su Zhu
category: Crypto hedge fund founder (Three Arrows Capital)
milestone_by_age_26: In 2012 at about age 24–25 he co-founded Three Arrows Capital (3AC) in San Francisco with Kyle Davies, raising ~$1M seed by borrowing from their parents.
early_history_summary: Born April 1987 in China; moved to the US at age 6. Graduated Phillips Academy Andover (~2005/2006) and Columbia University summa cum laude in mathematics. Worked as a derivatives trader at Credit Suisse, Flow Traders, and briefly Deutsche Bank before co-founding 3AC with childhood friend Davies in 2012.
family_context_summary: Immigrated from China to the US as a child; with Davies borrowed roughly $1M from parents to seed 3AC—evidence of family financial platform at founding.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a trading/finance family apprenticeship; parental capital seed is the clearest family advantage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Phillips Andover, Columbia math, parent seed capital, cofounder Davies, FX/derivatives trading seat
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and New York Magazine document April 1987 birth, Andover/Columbia path, Wall Street trading seats, and 2012 3AC founding with parent-borrowed seed. Fund later peaked near ~$10B AUM before 2022 collapse and Zhu’s 2023 Singapore arrest. Family domain coaching is not documented beyond capital; partner Davies is a durable complementary cofounder from prep school.
starting_point: Born April 1987 in China; moved to the United States at age 6 and later attended Phillips Academy Andover and Columbia University.
current_position: Former 3AC co-founder after 2022 fund collapse; later OPNX/crypto ventures; served prison time in Singapore (2023) for non-cooperation with liquidators.

trajectory.event: Graduated Columbia University summa cum laude in mathematics after Phillips Academy.
Co-founded Three Arrows Capital in San Francisco with Kyle Davies using ~$1M parent-borrowed seed.
Re-registered 3AC in Singapore; early focus on emerging-market FX derivatives arbitrage.
3AC failed margin calls and entered liquidation amid crypto crash; peak AUM had been estimated ~$10B.
Arrested at Singapore Changi Airport and imprisoned for failing to cooperate with liquidators.

name: Dennis Austin
milestone_by_age_26: Lead development of PowerPoint occurred 1985–1996 (ages ~38–49) after Forethought joined in late 1984; graduated UVA 1969 (~age 22) with ordinary early career at GE/Honeywell/Burroughs—no material independently verifiable breakout milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born May 28, 1947 in Pittsburgh; engineering at University of Virginia (1969) and graduate study at ASU, MIT, and UCSB. Career path through GE, Honeywell, Burroughs, Xerox PARC, and Gavilan before Forethought/PowerPoint.
family_context_summary: Father ran an executives' association; mother was a typist then homemaker in Rosslyn Farms, PA.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not a software/domain apprenticeship path; ordinary middle-class professional household.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Washington Post place birth 1947, UVA 1969, and PowerPoint lead role from mid-1980s—well after age 26. No dated material milestone by 26 identified beyond standard education and entry-level industry jobs.

name: Patrick Lewis
milestone_by_age_26: Lead author of the 2020 RAG paper while a FAIR PhD student at UCL, but no verified birth year found; cannot confirm the milestone occurred at age ≤26—marked ineligible under strict age rule.
early_history_summary: Known as lead author of the 2020 Retrieval-Augmented Generation paper (Facebook AI Research / UCL) and later leads RAG-related work at Cohere. Public bios do not document birth year or early family path.
evidence_summary: ArXiv RAG paper (2020) and NVIDIA/Cohere interviews establish research contribution, but without a birth year age-at-milestone cannot be verified under the strict ≤26 rule.

name: Sebastien Pahl
milestone_by_age_26: Around 2008–2010 (while finishing EPITECH, ~age 22–24) he co-founded dotCloud with Solomon Hykes and Kamel Founadi; the company entered Y Combinator Summer 2010 and later became Docker Inc.
early_history_summary: Born in France, raised partly in Hamburg (French school), studied at EPITECH (promo 2009) where he met Hykes. Built early container/PaaS technology in Paris, then relocated for YC S10. Left after Series A (~late 2011); later Cloudflare, Mesosphere, Red Hat Operator Framework, and Opstrace.
family_context_summary: Born France, childhood in Hamburg; Hykes recounted Pahl’s father fronting plane-ticket money for the YC interview trip—limited but concrete family support. Broader wealth not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a software-industry family; modest travel support for YC interview noted in secondary accounts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: EPITECH + Hykes, early containers, YC S10, SF frontier move
evidence_summary: Docker Inc. history, Hykes’s farewell post, and Kubernetes Podcast interview establish co-founding of dotCloud with Hykes while Pahl finished EPITECH (promo 2009), YC S10, and early container work. Exact birth date is not public; ~1986 estimate from EPITECH class timing and peer age places founding well under 26. Family background otherwise sparse.
starting_point: Born in France; spent much of childhood in Hamburg, Germany; studied intensive coding at EPITECH in France.
current_position: Senior Principal Systems Engineer at Cloudflare; previously co-founded Opstrace and worked at Red Hat, Mesosphere, and Cloudflare after leaving Docker/dotCloud.

trajectory.event: Co-founded dotCloud in Paris with Solomon Hykes and Kamel Founadi while finishing EPITECH studies.
dotCloud accepted into Y Combinator Summer 2010 and relocated to the US.
dotCloud raised Series A; Pahl left months later and soon joined early Cloudflare.
dotCloud rebranded around the Docker open-source project as Docker Inc.
Co-founded observability startup Opstrace after roles at Mesosphere and Red Hat.

name: Divya Gokulnath
milestone_by_age_26: In 2011 at age 24 she co-founded Byju's in Bangalore with Byju Raveendran after several years teaching in his test-prep classes.
early_history_summary: Born April 21, 1987 in Bengaluru; father Indian Air Force Wing Commander, mother Doordarshan programming executive. B.Tech Biotechnology at RV College of Engineering (2007), met Byju as GRE instructor, began teaching at 21 (2008), and co-founded the edtech company in 2011.
family_context_summary: Only child in Bengaluru; father IAF Wing Commander, mother Doordarshan programming executive—stable middle-class professional household with academic emphasis.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father taught her science as a child; not an edtech business inheritance but some parental academic coaching.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Byju partnership, early teaching reps, Bangalore, IAF/Doordarshan professional family
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Fortune India agree on 1987 birth, 2008 teaching start at 21, and 2011 Byju's co-founding at 24. Family is professional middle-class with light science coaching; primary early advantages are domain immersion as teacher and durable partnership with Byju Raveendran. Later COVID-era growth and billionaire-family status came after age 26.
starting_point: Born 21 April 1987 in Bengaluru to an Indian Air Force Wing Commander father and Doordarshan programming executive mother.
current_position: Co-founder of Byju's; public edtech leader amid company financial/governance turmoil in the mid-2020s.

trajectory.event: Completed B.Tech in Biotechnology at RV College of Engineering; met Byju Raveendran as GRE instructor.
Began teaching mathematics, English, and logical reasoning in large auditorium-style classes.
Co-founded Byju's with Byju Raveendran in Bangalore.
Led UX/content/brand efforts during COVID free-access surge; family listed among India's richest on Forbes.
Appointed chair of FICCI EdTech Taskforce.

name: TJ Holowaychuk
milestone_by_age_26: In 2010 at about age 23 he created Express.js (initial versions early 2010; v1 later that year), which became the dominant Node.js web framework.
early_history_summary: Canadian developer who became a prolific Node.js ecosystem author (Express, Connect, Mocha, Jade/Pug, Stylus, Commander, and hundreds of npm packages ~2009–2014) while working remotely at LearnBoost. Later shifted toward Go and self-funded tools (Apex).
primary_leverage_engine: Scarce open-source technical depth + platform-native distribution
primary_early_advantage_tags: npm/GitHub distribution, Node wave, extreme output volume
evidence_summary: Express.js Wikipedia and Node community histories date Express creation to 2010; CSV birth year 1987 implies age ~23. Contemporary profiles describe him as ~26 during the 2011–2012 LearnBoost peak productivity period. Family background is undocumented; leverage is almost entirely self-created OSS reputation on the early Node platform wave.
starting_point: Canadian software developer; early life and family class not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Independent engineer/entrepreneur after leaving Node for Go and cloud tooling (Apex and later projects); less public Node.js presence post-2014.

trajectory.event: Created Express.js, which became the standard minimal Node.js web framework.
Produced a large share of early Node ecosystem packages (Mocha, Jade, Stylus, Connect) while at LearnBoost.
Published farewell-to-Node essay and shifted primary work toward Go.
Built and promoted Apex and related serverless/Go tooling as independent founder.

name: Andrew Trader
milestone_by_age_26: Wharton undergrad class of 1991 implies birth ~1969; first major founding milestone Coremetrics (~1999, age ~30) and Zynga (2007, age ~38) both after 26—no material by-26 milestone found.
early_history_summary: Wharton BSE ~1991 and later MBA; co-founded Coremetrics (acq. IBM), Tribe.net (acq. Cisco), Zynga (2007 founding team), and Madison Reed; later investor/operating partner (Maveron, Bullpen Capital).
evidence_summary: Wharton Magazine lists Andrew Trader as W91 WG99; Crunchbase notes Entrepreneurial Management 1987–1991. Coremetrics and Zynga founding dates fall well after age 26. No earlier material milestone dated to ≤26 was found.

name: Karina Nguyen
milestone_by_age_26: By about age 23–24 (Claude 3 era, 2023–2024) she led post-training and evaluation work on Anthropic's Claude 3 models; earlier twenties also included design/engineering at Square, Dropbox, and the New York Times.
early_history_summary: Self-described as spending the first half of her twenties on Claude and ChatGPT. Path through product design/engineering (Square, Dropbox, NYT) into Anthropic post-training leadership, then OpenAI research on GPT-4o, Canvas, Tasks, and o-series reasoning models. By March 2026 she publicly stated she was 25 and founding/operating Thoughtful Lab after OpenAI.
primary_leverage_engine: Frontier lab post-training craft + product taste
primary_early_advantage_tags: Anthropic/OpenAI frontier labs, design-to-research path, Bay Area AI wave
evidence_summary: Lenny's Newsletter and her March 2026 Substack state Anthropic Claude 3 post-training leadership and later OpenAI product/research contributions while she was still in her early/mid-20s (age 25 as of Mar 2026). Exact birthdate not public; year estimated from that self-report. Family background undocumented; advantage is primarily frontier-lab immersion during the generative AI wave.
starting_point: Not fully documented; early career as designer/engineer at Square, Dropbox, and the New York Times before frontier AI labs.
current_position: Former OpenAI research lead; building Thoughtful Lab and writing publicly on post-training and AI product (as of 2026).

trajectory.event: Joined Anthropic (NYC) and began post-training/evaluation work on Claude models.
Credited with leading post-training and evaluation for Claude 3 models at Anthropic.
Moved to OpenAI; contributed to GPT-4o, Canvas, Tasks, and o-series reasoning models.
Left OpenAI path to focus on Thoughtful Lab and independent research/product work.

name: Jon Bentley
milestone_by_age_26: In 1975 at age 22 he published the seminal k-d tree paper 'Multidimensional binary search trees used for associative searching' (CACM), developed around his Stanford B.S. work; PhD UNC Chapel Hill followed in 1976 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born February 20, 1953 in Long Beach, California. B.S. mathematical sciences Stanford 1974; M.S./Ph.D. UNC Chapel Hill 1976. Early internships at Xerox PARC and SLAC. Later CMU faculty, Bell Labs, and Programming Pearls column/books.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford undergrad research, UNC PhD at 23, PARC/SLAC internships, k-d tree
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and the 1975 CACM paper establish k-d trees at age 22 and PhD at 23. Later Bell Labs and Programming Pearls cemented field stature. Family background not documented; primary early advantages are elite CS training and early research publication.
starting_point: Born February 20, 1953 in Long Beach, California; trained in mathematical sciences at Stanford.
current_position: American computer scientist known for algorithms and Programming Pearls; long career at Bell Labs/Avaya; still cited for k-d trees and geometric algorithms.

trajectory.event: Earned B.S. in mathematical sciences from Stanford University.
Published the foundational k-d tree paper in Communications of the ACM.
Completed Ph.D. at UNC Chapel Hill on divide-and-conquer closest-point algorithms.
Published Writing Efficient Programs and moved from CMU faculty to Bell Labs research.
Published Programming Pearls, collected from his CACM column.
Received Dr. Dobb's Excellence in Programming award.

name: Nick Frosst
milestone_by_age_26: In 2019 at age 26 he co-founded Cohere with Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang after serving as an early Geoffrey Hinton hire at Google Brain Toronto (from 2016, age 23).
early_history_summary: Born January 5, 1993 in Canada. B.S. computer science and cognitive science at University of Toronto (2015), student of Geoffrey Hinton, hired early at Google Brain Toronto (2016–2020). Co-founded enterprise LLM company Cohere in 2019; also lead singer of indie band Good Kid (formed 2015).
primary_leverage_engine: Elite mentor pipeline (Hinton/Google Brain) + cofounder team
family_context_summary: Canadian; detailed family class/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hinton student, Google Brain Toronto, UofT, Gomez/Zhang cofounders, LLM wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and TechCrunch document 1993 birth, UofT, Hinton/Google Brain path, and 2019 Cohere co-founding at age 26. Complementary founders (Gomez of Attention Is All You Need; Zhang) and Toronto AI ecosystem are well attested. Family wealth not documented; mentor and peer-team advantages are strong.
starting_point: Born January 5, 1993 in Canada; studied computer science and cognitive science at the University of Toronto under Geoffrey Hinton's influence.
current_position: Co-founder of Cohere (enterprise LLMs; multi-billion valuation) and lead singer of indie rock band Good Kid.

trajectory.event: Graduated University of Toronto (CS + cognitive science) and formed indie band Good Kid with classmates.
Joined Google Brain Toronto as an early machine-learning researcher under Geoffrey Hinton.
Co-founded Cohere with Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang to build enterprise large language models.
Cohere co-founders ranked among Maclean's AI Trailblazers as the company scaled enterprise LLM products.
Good Kid nominated for a Juno Award while Cohere continued large fundraising and enterprise growth.
